title: ClickFix has never been bigger, and AI tools are its most convincing lure yet
content_md: ClickFix has fast become one of the go-to techniques for criminals since it first emerged around 2024. It’s grown in both volume and variety, with an ever-expanding family of sub-techniques like FileFix, InstallFix, TerminalFix, and the entirely browser-native ConsentFix. The lures too have become more developed and targeted, with recent attacks preferring to target people searching for and using AI tools, a trick that is catching many users off guard and blending in with otherwise legitimate traffic for approved GenAI tools. Push's detection data shows how far the technique has spread. Through Q2 2026, ClickFix made up an average of 52% of Push's detections , overtaking AiTM and device code phishing for the first time, and in August that figure reached 67%. Across all the browser-based attacks Push intercepts, 1 in 2 arrive through channels other than email , such as search engines and social media. The rest came through email but weren’t stopped at the email gateway. ClickFix goes a step further: 4 in 5 ClickFix pages intercepted in 2026 were reached from search engines — through compromised websites, malvertising, and SEO poisoning. The latest ClickFix variants use AI tools as the bait. In Push's last quarterly snapshot, AI-themed InstallFix and LLMshare attacks made up around 5% of all attacks Push detected, a growing subset of the ClickFix family.
